# Additions to Esther Chapter 5 (Addition E) — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther E | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_005_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition E: The counter-decree in favor of the Jews. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 8:12.]*

**1** The following is a copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes sends greetings to the governors of the provinces from India to Ethiopia — one hundred and twenty-seven provinces — and to all who are well-disposed toward our affairs.

**2** Many who have been repeatedly honored by the extraordinary generosity of their benefactors have grown arrogant and sought not only to oppress those who are subject to our rule, but, unable to bear good fortune, have even plotted against those very people who showed them kindness.

**3** Not only have they driven out gratitude from among humanity, but, swollen with the empty boasts of those who know nothing of goodness, they imagined they could escape the ever-watchful judgment of God who hates evil.

**4** Often those placed in positions of authority have been made complicit in innocent bloodshed, drawn in by the persuasive words of friends entrusted with their affairs, and so have been implicated in irreversible misfortune through the malice of deception.

**5** One can observe the lying machinations of ill-disposed men not so much in the ancient stories handed down to us, as by looking at the wicked deeds that have happened even in recent times before our own eyes,

**6** and so to guard better for the future, that we may render the kingdom undisturbed and peaceful for all people,

**7** by making necessary reforms and judging what comes to our attention always with more equitable decisions.

**8** For Haman son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian by birth and foreign to the Persian blood, and estranged from our benevolence — receiving our hospitality and enjoying the kindness we extend to every nation to such a degree as to be called our father and honored by all as second after the royal throne —

**9** was unable to restrain his arrogance, and schemed to deprive us of both our kingdom and our life.

**10** Through fabricated intrigues and tricks, he sought the destruction of Mordecai, our preserver and continual benefactor, and of Esther, the blameless partner of our kingdom, together with their entire nation.

**11** For by these means he thought, when we had been stripped of our allies, to transfer the rule of the Persians to the Macedonians.

**12** But we find that the Jews are not evildoers, but are governed by the most just of laws,

**13** and are sons of the Most High, the great living God, who has guided the kingdom in the most excellent manner, both for us and for our ancestors.

**14** You will therefore do well not to give effect to the letters sent by Haman son of Hammedatha,

**15** since the man who devised these things has been hanged at the gates of Susa with all his household — God, who rules over all, having swiftly given him the judgment he deserved.

**16** Post copies of this letter publicly everywhere,

**17** and permit the Jews to follow their own customs, and assist them, so that on that very day — the thirteenth of the twelfth month, that is Adar — they may defend themselves against those who attack them at the time of their oppression.

**18** For God, who rules all things, has turned this day for them from destruction of the chosen race into joy.

**19** Therefore, among your celebrated festivals, keep this day too with all gladness,

**20** so that both now and hereafter it may be for us and for those who are loyal to the Persians an occasion of salvation, and for those who plot against us a memorial of destruction.

**21** Every city or country that does not act according to these things shall be devastated with fire and wrath — rendered not only inaccessible to human beings but also utterly loathsome to wild animals and birds for all time."
